resources.string: Handles code, files, and documents and suits most tasks. The agent uses search, editing, and terminal tools as needed.

### How it works

Agent calls tools directly to read and write files, search material, and run terminal commands. It includes Skills, plans, goals, sub-agents, workflows, and context compaction.

### When to choose it

Everyday coding, file work, and document organization can start here. Standard mode can also write scripts and batch-process files; PTC changes how tools are called, so batch tasks do not require PTC.

### Fix a problem

> After the search form was submitted twice in a row, the results disappeared. Find the cause, fix the problem, run the relevant tests, and explain the cause and the changes.

Expected output: code changes, relevant test results, and an explanation of the cause.

### Organize project notes

> Read the Markdown notes in the project, summarize the conclusions already reached and the questions still open, and link the corresponding files.

Expected output: a summary with source references that can be checked against the originals.
Includes every capability of standard mode and is better suited to tasks that call tools in bulk and then filter, organize, deduplicate, count, or summarize the results.

### How tools are called

PTC is Programmatic Tool Calling: tools are called from a program. The current built-in preset has the agent write TypeScript programs with run_code that call the generated tool SDK. Programs can organize loops, conditionals, error handling, and calls that benefit from concurrency.

### What reaches the model

Tool results go to the program first, where they are filtered, computed, or merged, and then reach the model through output or return values; image results are attached separately. Tool calls in the program are still recorded and still bound by tool permissions.

### Difference from standard mode

Both modes can program and batch-process files. Standard mode gives each tool to the model directly; PTC lets the model organize tool calls in code. The current PTC preset does not enable the workflow tool. Speed and token usage depend on the task and how results are handled.

### Batch-check configuration files

> Check every JSON file under configs/ and use schema.json to find missing fields and invalid values. Write each issue as one row in a CSV; also record files that cannot be read in the report and continue with the remaining files. Keep the original files.

Expected output: a list of issues and a CSV report. A program can run the same checks over many files, handle a failure on a single file, and then merge the results.

### Summarize error logs

> Analyze the logs under logs/, count occurrences by service and error type, list the ten most frequent error types, and keep one example for each. Save the complete statistics as a separate CSV.

Expected output: a summary of frequent errors and the complete statistics table. Intermediate data can be aggregated in the program first, then the summary handed to the model.
The agent uses a terminal and an image-reading tool with context compaction, which suits testing and comparing its baseline behavior.

### What is kept

Provides a persistent shell and the read_image tool with a fixed system prompt. Reading images requires a model that supports image input. Earlier history is compacted automatically when context pressure reaches a threshold; while the agent is idle you can enter /compact to compact manually. The built-in preset does not load Skills or plans and does not inject the standard runtime context.

### When to choose it

Useful as a baseline for experiments and comparison tests. The agent can still read and write files and run scripts through terminal commands, but it lacks built-in support for managing long tasks. Fewer tools do not make it easier for beginners.

### Compare basic repair behavior

> Run the tests for this project, find the cause of the failures, make the smallest fix, then run the relevant tests again and report the results.

Run this task in standard mode and in minimal mode from the same workspace state, and compare completion, tool calls, and the final changes. Minimal mode performs these operations through terminal commands.
Customize DSH through conversation: have the agent write plugins that add features or UI, and combine tools and prompts to create your own modes.

### What you can create

Creator mode has the standard task tools plus runtime inspection, persistent plugin management, and development guidance for Cordis plugins and agent presets. You can write plugins to add features or UI, and combine tools and prompts to create modes for specific tasks.

### How plugins and modes relate

Plugins add capabilities to DSH, such as tools, service connections, or UI entry points. A mode is an agent preset that selects the tools available for a task and sets how the agent works. Custom modes can also use plugins that you develop.

### How to make results take effect

You can ask the agent to complete the installation and verify the actual result. Plugins may load immediately or need a restart depending on what changed; a newly created mode is selected when a new task is created.

### Add a UI

> Help me write a DSH plugin that adds a Project Notes entry to the sidebar, lists the Markdown files in the current workspace, and previews content when clicked. Complete the installation and verify that the page opens.

Expected output: a plugin with a sidebar entry and a preview page, plus any effect steps still required.

### Add a tool

> Write a plugin that provides a tool to read the project test report and summarize failing cases. Register the tool and verify the call with a sample report.

Expected output: a new callable tool and the verified result of one sample call.

### Create your own mode

> Create a Code Review mode based on standard mode that prioritizes potential bugs and test gaps, cites files and line numbers, and asks me before modifying files. Save it as a selectable preset.

Expected output: a custom mode that can be selected for a new task. The review requirements guide the agent, while the operations actually allowed are still determined by permission settings.
